title: Support Census metadata and keyed sample requests
objective: Census product/vintage/geography metadata and key requirements are explicit without placing secrets in evidence URLs, browser assets or model inputs.
outcome: ACS five-year, ACS one-year and time-series fixtures remain distinct with no false observation-period inference. A Census key may be received only through the existing secret-provider port. Missing keys produce a documented access step. Keyless HTML remains authentication-required. Keyed fixture succeeds and retained logs redact query credentials. Geography hierarchy, allowed predicates and variable labels/concepts are parsed without treating them as definitions. A bounded sample recipe is emitted only when required inputs are satisfied.

commits.subject: Resolve Census metadata links
commits.instructions: Bind variables, geography, groups, examples and vintage links to exact catalog entries. Preserve aggregate versus microdata products and rolling series.
commits.verification: ACS five-year, ACS one-year and time-series fixtures remain distinct, with no false observation-period inference.

commits.subject: Add a source-scoped credential adapter
commits.instructions: Allow the collector to receive a Census key through the existing secret-provider port; never place it in evidence URLs, browser assets or model inputs. Missing keys produce a documented access step.
commits.verification: The audit’s keyless HTML response remains authentication-required; keyed fixture succeeds and all retained logs redact query credentials.

commits.subject: Extract documented query dimensions
commits.instructions: Parse geography hierarchy, allowed predicates and variable labels/concepts without treating them as definitions. Emit a bounded sample recipe only when required inputs are satisfied.
commits.verification: A Pennsylvania aggregate example uses its exact supported variables/geography and records the source’s required access conditions.
